'''Kanazawa Gosha''' (金沢五社) is the collective term for the five Yoshida Shinto shrines located in {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|en|Ishikawa Prefecture|qid=Q131281|lt=Ishikawa Prefecture|1=Ishikawa Prefecture}} and {{ill|Kanazawa|en|Kanazawa|qid=Q191130|lt=Kanazawa City|1=Kanazawa}}, namely, {{ill|Utasu Shrine|ja|宇多須神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utasu Shrine|1=Utasu Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q125927189}}, Kosaka Shrine, Shinmeigu Shrine, Tsubakihara Tenmangu, and Yasue Hachimangu of Yoshida Shinto.

All five shrines were Ranked as prefectural shrines under the modern {{ill|Shrine Ranking system|ja|社格|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Ranking system|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Shakaku|qid=Q10444029}} system. Visiting all five shrines was known as "Gosha-mairi" and was widely practiced.

== Utasu Shrine (宇多須神社) ==
[[File:Utasu.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Utasu Shrine]]
'''{{ill|Utasu Shrine|ja|宇多須神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utasu Shrine|1=Utasu Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q125927189}}''' was founded in 718 ({{ill|Yōrō|en|Yōrō|qid=Q1373061|lt=Yōrō|1=Yōrō}} 2). In 1599 ({{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keichō|1=Keichō}} 4) it secretly enshrined {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|qid=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie|1=Maeda Toshiie}}, with retainers contributing their ritual fees according to their stipends. With the founding of {{ill|Oyama Shrine (Ishikawa)|en|Oyama Shrine (Ishikawa)|qid=Q998709|lt=Oyama Shrine|1=Oyama Shrine (Ishikawa)}}, the original enshrined deity, {{ill|Takamimusubi|en|Takamimusubi|qid=Q125400|lt=Takami Musubi|1=Takamimusubi}}, was transferred.

Location: Kanazawa City Higashiyama 1-chōme 30-8

== Kosaka Shrine (小坂神社) ==
[[File:Kosakajinja.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Kosaka Shrine]]
'''Kosaka Shrine''' was founded in 717 (the first year of the Yōrō era) on land that had once been a manor ({{ill|Manorialism|en|Manorialism|qid=Q1550557|lt=Manor|1=Manorialism}}) of {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|Kasuga-taisha|qid=Q714559|lt=Kasuga Taisha|1=Kasuga-taisha}}<ref>[https://www4.city.kanazawa.lg.jp/11104/bunkazaimain/shiteibunkazai/yukeikenzou/kosakajinnjya.html Kosaka Shrine Main Hall] - Kanazawa City</ref>. This shrine is also a branch shrine of Kasuga Taisha, affectionately known as "Kasuga-san". The main deities are {{ill|Ameno-Koyane|ja|アメノコヤネ|lt=Ameno Koyane-no-mikoto|lt_ja=天児屋根命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ameno-Koyane|qid=Q2564508|1=Ame-no-Koyane|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2564508}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|ja|経津主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1107286}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|Himegami|qid=Q22070227|lt=Hime-no-kami|1=Himegami}}, and {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|Takemikazuchi|qid=Q1502690|lt=Take Mikazuchi-no-ōkami|1=Takemikazuchi}}.

Location: Kanazawa City Yamanoue-chō 42-1

== Shinmeigu Shrine (神明宮) ==
'''Shinmeigu Shrine''' is one of Japan's Seven Shinmei Shrines, alongside {{ill|Shiba Taian Shrine|ja|芝大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiba Taian Shrine|1=Shiba Dai-jingū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11614619}} (Shiba Shinmeigu) in {{ill|港区|en|港区|qid=Q14219833|lt=Minato Ward, Tokyo|1=港区}}, {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|qid=Q1490|lt=Tokyo|1=Tokyo}}, and Higashi-Iwakura Shinmei (in {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q740246}}), among others. It is renowned for the "Aburimochi" ritual held in spring and autumn<ref>{{Cite news|url = https://www.hokurikushinkansen-navi.jp/pc/news/article.php?id=NEWS0000014703|title = あぶりもちで無病息災 金沢・神明宮で神事|publisher = 北陸新幹線で行こう!北陸・信越観光ナビ（北國新聞）|date = 2018-05-16|accessdate = 2019-10-12}}</ref>. The poem "Circus" by {{ill|Chūya Nakahara|en|Chūya Nakahara|qid=Q278215|lt=Chūya Nakahara|1=Chūya Nakahara}} was inspired by a circus he saw in the shrine's precincts during his childhood, and the shrine—located near the birthplace of {{ill|Murō Saisei|en|Murō Saisei|qid=Q331339|lt=Muro Saisei|1=Murō Saisei}}—has long been associated with poets. The main deities are {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|lt=Amaterasu-ōmikami|lt_ja=天照皇大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q455602}} and {{ill|Toyouke Omikami|ja|豊受姫大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Omikami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to トヨウケビメ|1=Toyouke-hime|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2983724}}.

Location: Kanazawa City Nomachi 2-chōme 1-8

== Tsubakihara Tenmangu (椿原天満宮) ==
[[File:Tsubakiharatenmanguu.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Tsubakihara Tenmangu]]
'''Tsubakihara Tenmangu''' was founded in 1297 ({{ill|Einin|en|Einin|qid=Q1327307|lt=Einin|1=Einin}} 5) by the guardian {{ill|Togashi Yoshichika|ja|富樫義親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Togashi Yoshichika|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} as one of the {{ill|Tenmangū|en|Tenmangū|qid=Q798838|lt=Choraku-ji Tenmangū|1=Tenmangū}}. It was relocated to its present site during the {{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|qid=Q1192913|lt=Kan'ei|1=Kan'ei}} period of the Edo period. The site of Tsubakihara Fort, occupied by Susaki Hyō during the {{ill|Ikkō-ikki|en|Ikkō-ikki|qid=Q947533|lt=Ikko-ikki|1=Ikkō-ikki}}, still remains. Nowadays, concerts—including chamber music, folk, rock, blues, and band performances—are frequently held in the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=Haiden|1=Haiden (Shinto)}} to great acclaim. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|en|Sugawara no Michizane|qid=Q382005|lt=Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane}}.

Location: Kanazawa City Tenjinchō 1-chōme 1-13

== Yasue Hachimangu (安江八幡宮) ==
[[File:Torii in front of Haiden of Yasue Hachiman Shrine.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Yasue Hachimangu]]
'''Yasue Hachimangu''' was founded in 939 ({{ill|Tengyō|en|Tengyō|qid=Q1327340|lt=Tenkei|1=Tengyō}} 2). It is also known as '''Kanazawa Suitengū''', and is the only {{ill|Suitengū|en|Suitengū|qid=Q125319456|lt=Suitengū Shrine|1=Suitengū}} enshrined in Ishikawa Prefecture.
[[File:Stone lantern and sculpture of Kaga-Hachiman Roly-poly doll in Yasue Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|200px|right|The statue of {{ill|Kaga Hachimakiagari|ja|加賀八幡起上り|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaga Hachimakiagari|1=Kaga Hachiman okiagari|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q28689012}} at Yasue Hachimangu]]
The local toy "Kaga Hachimakiagari" originated from being dedicated to this shrine, and Ishikawa Prefecture's mascot character, "Hyakumansan", is based on it. The main deities are {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|qid=Q317997|lt=Hotakeda-wake no Mikoto|1=Emperor Ōjin}} and {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|qid=Q232803|lt=Kinenadahime no Mikoto|1=Empress Jingū}}.

Location: Kanazawa City Konohanamachi 11-27
